text: That is why sometimes they go the extra mile – the suppliers and the vendors make the extra efforts to try to sell things to us – because DSTA does a thorough evaluation not only in terms of ability, but value for money.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The other significant aspect to stretch the defence dollar is through design from inception.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And there are many such examples where cost has been saved through maintenance or reduction in crew.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is the collective resolve and commitment of all Singaporeans, including Members of Parliament here, to build a strong SAF that protects our home and provides us assurance and space in this unpredictable world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, the Minister for Defence just spoke about how our geopolitical environment is becoming increasingly complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF must evolve with these challenges in order to be able to mount a strong national defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our greatest asset remains our people, with NS as the cornerstone of our defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF and the SAF must, therefore, continue to invest in capable NSmen, enrich their NS experience and strengthen Singaporean's support for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF is committed to training our NSmen effectively and safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We must and we will uphold the trust in us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked about improvements to training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: IGO inspectors go to each unit to assess the robustness of their safety systems as well as their practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They interview servicemen at every level – from commanders, to safety appointment holders, to soldiers – in order to understand how safety measures are practised on the ground and whether the soldiers themselves feel confident and comfortable to provide feedback on safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Safety audits aside, there must also be concrete, consistent action at all levels and at all times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Army has introduced 100% inspections of all high-risk activities and field training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Existing equipment are regularly reviewed, while new equipment are designed with inbuilt safety features.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For instance, the newly commissioned Hunter Armoured Fighting Vehicle comes with emergency stop features, as well as audio and visual alerts to prompt the crew about surrounding hazards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As Mr Arasu Duraisamy pointed out, we want every soldier to consciously keep safe while they train.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is not a compromise, it is both at the same time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To achieve this, unit commanders conduct before- and after-action reviews and risk assessments with the units as part of their daily work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The 6th Army Maintenance Base is an example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: During morning roll calls, their commanders and soldiers discuss openly about possible lapses or near-misses; for example, if you use the wrong tools or soldiers not wearing their helmets and so on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Using a simple Think-Check-Do approach, the soldiers systematically plan their steps, check their equipment and pre-empt risks before each maintenance task.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over time, every soldier will internalise these safety practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, I spoke about SafeGuardian, which is a one-stop mobile app for on-the-go access to safety checklists, instant sharing of hazards among servicemen and notification amongst them of danger zones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By placing safety information within the easy and instant reach of our servicemen, we foster a culture of safety – "By All, For All".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The app was trialed in our Naval Bases and feedback has been positive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will be progressively rolling this out throughout the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I have spoken so far about preventive measures to keep our soldiers safe as they train.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked how the SAF is improving its response to medical emergencies when accidents happen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: SAF Medics undergo an 11-week training on life-saving skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In other words, the SAF medics go with the SCDF paramedics in the ambulances attending to real cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By doing so, they put their knowledge into practice under real-life, time-pressured situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Recently, we also piloted the attachment of our medics to the National University Hospital (NUH) Emergency Medicine Department.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Such hands-on trainings are extremely valuable to our medics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They have emerged from such trainings more confident and competent in casualty management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Discussions are currently underway with both SCDF and the other hospitals to extend and expand such programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Through these various initiatives, we will build a capable fighting force that will always train effectively and safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Moving from safety to health, Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the precautionary measures that SAF has put in place to protect our servicemen in light of the COVID-19 threat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last week, we extended these measures to pre-enlistees and NSmen who have travelled to Daegu City or to Cheongdo County in South Korea, in line with MOH's revised advisory.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In other words, we keep a very, very close eye on the situation and we adjust accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: All SAF Medical Centres have a Pandemic Readiness Response Plan and we hold sufficient supplies of Personal Protective Equipment and we also have medical personnel ready to manage suspected cases in line with MOH's requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to do our utmost to protect our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: While our robust training and safety measures and medical support give our soldiers the confidence to train well and to train hard, the enduring strength of the SAF ultimately rests on the commitment on the part of our soldiers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is why we constantly look for ways to improve the NS experience for every serviceman at every stage of his NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This point was raised by Mr Chong Kee Hiong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For pre-enlistees, we are preparing them better for NS, both physically and mentally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As Mr Chong Kee Hiong pointed out, our pre-enlistees come from diverse backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For the vast majority obviously are still citizens born and bred in Singapore and who, as Members have pointed out, most likely have family members who had undergone NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Yet, there are also new citizens and PRs who may not have family or friends who have undergone NS before.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In other words, they may know less, compared to Singaporeans who were born and bred here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are also facilitating mutual learning and exchange among NS coordinators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In one such exchange, which was hosted by the United World College (South East Asia) last year, I was there and the discussions were very enriching, frank and open.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: There will be another round upcoming and I look forward to attending it as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are also aware that many pre-enlistees want to be more physically prepared before they enter NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Hence, MINDEF is collaborating with the Singapore Armed Forces Reservists Association (SAFRA) to make gym facilities more accessible through the Pre-Enlistees Exercise Programme for NS (PREP4NS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are also looking at increasing more venues and, for this, we are now working with SportSG in order to see how best to give membership access to its 24 gyms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: More details on this will be provided later when we are clearer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSFs devote two full years to serving the nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is, therefore, incumbent upon us as stewards of their time and talents to make sure that we support their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, take, for instance, the Vocational Interest initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This was started in 2016 and, under this initiative, NSFs may indicate their interest in 33 NS vocations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: What MINDEF, SAF do is, we do our best to match them as far as possible to the vocation of their choice, subject to, obviously, our operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are encouraged to see that more than 60% indicate interest in demanding vocations, such as in Infantry, Guards, Armour, and strong interest by our NSFs to also become commanders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These courses range from SkillsFuture Series courses, to those offered by institutes of higher learning (IHLs) that will aid the NSFs in their admission or to gain them credit exemptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, for this year, we will be introducing further enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: First, NSFs can look forward to full subsidy of the E-PREP courses as opposed to currently allowing the E-PREP credits to fund up to 90%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Second, we will raise the number of E-PREP courses that are available, expand the pool of E-PREP courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I am excited to share that two new institutions are coming on board to offer E-PREP courses, namely, the National University of Singapore (NUS) and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), bringing the number of E-PREP partners to nine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For our existing E-PREP partners, we have also worked closely with them to expand their course offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With these additions, NSFs across the SAF and the Home Team will be able to enjoy a pool of some 4,000 courses, up 1,000 from last year, from 1 April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Out of these, close to 100 will be credit-bearing as they undertake further studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, depending on what is your current rank, level, vocation and your deployment, it will go up by between $70 and $120.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will be applicable to NSFs and NSmen in both the SAF and the Home Team, covering all ranks and vocations from 1 March 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Douglas Foo brought this up and I thank him for that.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As we continue to place our NSmen at the heart of what we do, we also constantly ask ourselves: how can we serve ever more efficiently and effectively?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is why we are applying digital technologies to various facets of NS, from administration and training to healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about this, so allow me to share some information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For our servicemen, their NS journey begins at the Central Manpower Base (CMPB).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over the years, we have enhanced the experience at CMPB for pre-enlistees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A real-time queue management system and facial recognition technology are also on trial for a more seamless experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For instance, pre-enlistees will be able to complete their bond and exit permit application in one single online application and transaction instead of the separate applications and transactions that they currently have to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Pre-enlistees will also be able to monitor the progress of their applications online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Under Virtual Care, medical officers in the SAF use technologies, such as digital stethoscopes and video conferencing tools, to diagnose effectively and prescribe medicine for common ailments remotely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, this service was piloted at two SAF medical centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It has proven to be convenient, it actually also allows the diagnosis to be done faster because you do not have to wait for the doctor and the patient to physically meet as applied to common ailments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, this has made medical services more accessible, more convenient and has reduced wait times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I have just spoken about MINDEF and the SAF's efforts to provide the best possible experience for every NSman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As Mr Ang Hin Kee highlighted, our families, businesses, schools and community groups are also key pillars of support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Through ACCORD, we will continue to appreciate and rally strong societal support for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: My deepest appreciation to ACCORD members, especially for contributing their ideas and for so proactively putting their initiatives into action within their respective communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The business community, for example, has stepped up to show appreciation for our soldiers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Earlier, Mr Douglas Foo has also elaborated on what the SMF, as a business federation, has done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Amongst them is Mr Anthony Low, hawker-owner and Chairman of Boon Lay Hawker’s Association.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, what Mr Low did was he rallied more than 60 hawker stalls within his Association's membership to provide privileges to NSmen, after seeing how his son had toughened up through NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In so many different and individual ways, we can make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, every effort and every gesture counts and it is appreciated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To thank the businesses for their support, we held the inaugural "We Support NS" Appreciation Function last year and we thanked more than 200 merchants who came to meet us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We hope that the momentum can be kept up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Likewise, ACCORD has engaged the communities – different communities – in multiple ways to continue fostering wide and deep support for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, this journey never ends and, in the context of what was discussed, the need for Total Defence in all its dimensions is something that we have to keep doing and press on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, through continued whole-of-society commitment to our defence, we will demonstrate our will and resolve to protect Singapore's freedom and sovereignty, come what may.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, the strength of a nation depends largely on the readiness of her people to resist and respond to the threats, and there are various manifestations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These demands and all-round defence and a deterrent strategy are best provided by Total Defence, with its six pillars and emphasis on everyone playing their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Total Defence has rallied Singaporeans together in responding to challenges that have threatened our independence and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite these challenges, be it threats from terrorism, economic downturns and SARS, we overcame them all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The outbreak of COVID-19 is the latest test of our collective strength as a nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked how Singaporeans can play a part to overcome this crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the past month, we have seen how fear of the virus had led to panic buying of household essentials, hoarding and profiteering from the sale of masks and shunning of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Yet at the same time, we came across countless heartwarming examples of how Singaporeans have displayed quiet strength and resolve to fight this crisis together, of residents leaving hand sanitisers and spare masks in common areas for others, and university students bringing food for their classmates who were on leave of absence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Religious leaders have also come together to provide religious guidance during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), for example, has said in an advisory to Muslims that Islam excuses those who are unwell from attending congregational prayers, including Friday prayers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Muslims are also advised to set aside the practice of salam or shaking hands to ensure that they do not transmit the virus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some temples and churches are scaling back or cancelling regular services and urging followers to watch their services online instead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I really appreciate the guidance provided by the religious leaders to rally the community together in the current situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Government is mindful that Singaporeans and businesses are facing pressures as Singapore is affected by economic downturn, slow-down and uncertainties from this COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is heartening to know that the businesses are exemplifying economic defence by implementing business continuity plans, sending workers for retraining and following calls to disinfect working areas regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hopefully, these measures will provide workers with greater job assurance and help them cope and emerge stronger from the difficult period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As businesses do their part, fellow Singaporeans should also show solidarity and take the necessary precautions and carry on with our own life; eat and shop as you normally do and support these businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Please do not panic when you see shops disinfecting their premises or medical workers in Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) providing assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These practices are routine precautionary procedures at a time like this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we fight the virus, concurrently, we are also fighting an even greater threat, the spread of fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When you receive messages or unsubstantiated information over WhatsApp or other online platforms, do not forward or circulate them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Always check the information against official sources like the Government websites or the official news releases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If you are unsure, do not spread the information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such discipline will go a long way in our fight against fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All in all, Singapore can and will overcome this COVID-19 situation if Singaporeans are psychologically resilient and support the Government and businesses to deal with this outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should not be easily rattled and instead show confidence as a people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As my soldiers often say in Hokkien "ai zai" or be steady.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, may I say a few words in Malay, please?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Religious leaders in Singapore have come together to provide religious guidance and to prepare measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, MUIS had advised Muslims in Singapore that, in Islam, those who are unwell are excused from attending congregational prayers, including Friday prayers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Muslims were also advised to set aside the practice of "salam" to avoid the transmission of the virus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some temples and churches in Singapore are scaling back or suspending mass and regular services, and urging followers to watch their services online instead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I really appreciate the guidance provided by the religious leaders to rally the community together in this current situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we try to prevent the transmission of this virus, there is an even greater threat that we must fight, that is, the spread of fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: According to an MIT study, fake news can travel six times faster than true stories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the past month, false information on the closure of schools and an MRT station due to the spread of COVID-19 was propagated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is important to remember that, whenever you receive messages or unsubstantiated information over WhatsApp or other social media platforms, please do not forward or circulate them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Please ensure that you check the information you receive against official sources, like the Government websites and official news releases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If you are unsure, do not spread the information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have to be disciplined in the fight against fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All in all, Singapore can and will overcome this COVID-19 situation if Singaporeans are ready, psychologically resilient and support the efforts by the Government and businesses to deal with this outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should not be easily rattled, and instead be confident as a people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As my soldiers often say "Relax, Don't Be Stressed Out!" (In English): Mr Chairman, the spread of falsehoods during this COVID-19 crisis is just one example of how fake news can damage our society, erode communal trust and social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how MINDEF is supporting the whole-of-Government efforts to prepare Singaporeans to combat the spread of online falsehoods and fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The enhancement to the programme will equip participants with the skills to detect and deal with fake news and digital threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students who joined the 2019 N.E.mation! competition had the chance to visit the SAF Cyber Defence School, which equips the MINDEF/SAF's cyber workforce with skillsets and knowledge for deployment in cyber defence entities, to learn about the SAF's cyber capabilities and contributions to keep Singapore's network systems and infrastructure safe and secure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They also visited The Straits Times’ (ST's) newly revamped newsroom to learn how ST detects and deals with fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Online falsehoods can also affect the reputation and credibility of businesses and even cause serious financial losses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last January, Tesla's shares and consumers' confidence in their products were affected when fake videos claiming that Tesla's cars were unsafe were circulated online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about the initiatives targeted at business owners to equip them to deal with digital threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We conducted one session last year and the feedback on this has been very positive so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we do our utmost to defend Singapore against digital threats, we have to acknowledge that it is impossible to prevent all cyber and data incidents, especially by determined and capable adversaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about MINDEF's efforts to strengthen cybersecurity against potential threats and attacks on our security systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MINDEF/SAF is doubling down on efforts to raise the cybersecurity standards and readiness within the entire defence sector, including our vendors and among MINDEF-related organisations like SAFRA and the National Service Resort and Country Club (NSRCC).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will limit the amount of data they hold and ensure implementation of technical and procedural measures to protect the data during transmission and storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: DCSC will coordinate operations across the defence sector and integrate cyber threat intelligence capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we step up efforts in digital defence, the multifaceted threats of today mean that to keep Singapore strong, we need the collective efforts of all aspects of society – the Government, businesses, communities and individuals like you and me – across every Total Defence pillar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked about MINDEF's efforts to engage the community to strengthen resilience against potential threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MINDEF is working with the People's Association (PA) to introduce the Total Defence Achiever Badge programme this year for the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT), which currently includes 2,000 active volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To achieve the highest tier of this programme, CERT volunteers will have to attend lessons to learn how to identify fake news, community mediation and psychological first aid, among other training components.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this way, CERT volunteers will be better equipped with the knowledge and skills to respond to the evolving nature of emergencies, thereby putting Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin also asked for an update about the Government-led and community-led efforts to strengthen Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As noted by Ms Joan Pereira, in many countries, education on the importance of resilience and emergency preparedness starts at a young age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In Singapore, to anchor Total Defence for our next generation, MINDEF collaborated with Mediacorp artiste Edmund Chen and the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) to create "My Little Red Dot – Making Our Home A Better Place" book.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through this book, young children can learn about Total Defence in an interactive manner and parents are encouraged to share values, such as unity and resilience, with their children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, key to Total Defence is a strong SAF – our Military Defence pillar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For a small country like Singapore, the only way to have a credible military of sufficient size is to have a conscript force, where every able-bodied male Singaporean defends Singapore, thereby contributing to Military Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Earlier, Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How had talked about this extensively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I believe that strong family and societal support for our NSmen will motivate them to give of their best when performing their duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This allows significant cost savings because servicemen no longer need to pay individual membership fees for each dependant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that this will encourage more families to visit SAFRA and HomeTeamNS clubhouses, enjoy the facilities and spend more quality time together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SAFRA and HomeTeamNS will announce more details on this in mid-2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last month, we launched the new Total Defence logo, the winning design by Ms Samantha Teng, an Allied Educator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the significance of the new logo and how Singaporeans responded to the call for the design of this new logo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In Ms Teng’s design, the arrows pointing upwards represent Singapore’s continuous journey to stay resilient against current and future threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Global trends and threats are evolving and, as Mr Seah Kian Peng noted, one of the issues our youths and many young people around the world are increasingly concerned with is climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given that Total Defence has kept Singapore strong for more than 35 years, it is timely for us, as a nation, to revitalise this all-round defence and deterrence strategy to address these threats confronting Singapore now and in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue partnering fellow Singaporeans to seek ideas on how to strengthen our Total Defence because this should be a whole-of-nation effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will also allow younger Singaporeans to reflect on what Total Defence is to them and operationalise this as we respond to future threats and challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must continue to encourage the community spirit shown during this period and support those at the frontlines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is with this collective strength that we are able to stay resilient and united as one people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must make Total Defence in every Singaporean's DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With a strong Total Defence, we have every reason to have confidence and a sense of hope for Singapore's future.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, two clarifications for the Minister for Defence regarding our purchase of the F-35s.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, the Minister mentioned that US Congressional approval has been obtained for the purchases.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Do I understand that this is the in-principle approval that is needed and that the formal terms of the sale and purchase are still being negotiated and finalised?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification concerns the Minister's acknowledgement that there had been some technical issues with the plane and he mentioned that to ensure that our defence dollars are well-spent, the timelines that are available to us will be useful.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Could he elaborate a bit more about this aspect?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: First, on the process which is specific to the US requirements, the US DoD has to support, which they have.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The administration has to support, which they did when we submitted our letter of request.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have said that we are in the final stages and we are.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For the second part of Ms Sylvia Lim's question, by the time we acquire it in 2026 or beyond – we have evaluated the first four F-35Bs that we have acquired and then made a decision – in production, you would probably have for F-35s and F35Bs across the world a few thousand platforms used by many, many militaries.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In other words, there are many vested interests for many countries which plan their air defence systems based on that acquisition.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: With new platforms, not only with the F-35s but also F-16s and F-15s, you will always have design issues, operational issues.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, the assessments, of course, will be done technically as well as with our pilots.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There are some issues related to maintenance and parts and so on, but that is logistics.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think most of the issues that were raised initially when the F-35 procurement was in its infancy would have been ironed out.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think the Minister mentioned there were three imminent threats: terrorism, cybersecurity and maritime threats, of which the most difficult to plan and deal with would be cyber.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But the current plan is for cybersecurity to be dealt with under the SAF and reporting to the CDF.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Would the Minister also consider having a force outside the SAF to deal with this, particularly so that it can tap on talent which may not want to be in the military, such as the white hats or people with talent in this area?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There are various agencies dealing, for example, with cyber threats.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For SAF, it would be similar to identifying threats as we do in the kinetic world, in the real world – air, land and sea.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In other words, if there are state and non-state actors who are using the cyber realm to first infiltrate, then to decimate, to diminish our will, as a precursor, for example, to a kinetic move, as we talked about, a hybrid.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: A few years ago, I mentioned to this House this concept of hybrid warfare, which was surfaced by some military experts.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We see it as the SAF's responsibility to identify these external threats.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, if there is a terrorist plot, first, to capture our population – not necessarily jihadists, it could be any religion – to capture acolytes for their movements, as a long-term plan or even a medium-term plan, we ought to be able to identify that.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And together with that, information warfare, then to gather arms or to have plots or to commit sabotage.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, there has to be a central role for the SAF, which is similar to what we have defined as our role in protecting Singapore's sovereignty and stability.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Now, having defined our missions, then, who do you need?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There are pros and cons, for example, even within the SAF and MINDEF context.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The comfort for any Minister, or indeed anybody who oversees the security for MINDEF and SAF, is that the SAF is the quickest to mobilise.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When you push a button, you know that the SAF can move.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Whereas other units, there is a little bit more discussion, I think.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think you know what we are talking about.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, there are these considerations which, over time, we will be able to address.

speaker: Mr Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It has been quite an interesting development in our SAF with all the threats evolving, and we would also wish to thank our men and women in uniform who serve and protect us.
